newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak 96 sugar production rises to 226,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Slovak 96 sugar production rises to 226,000 tonnes.

text.p: Slovakia produced around 226,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996, some 68,000 tonnes more than the previous year, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Friday.
Stefan Palacka, head of the ministry's plant production department, told Reuters that Slovakia might export between 20,000 and 25,000 tonnes of sugar of the 1996 output.

He added that for the first time since the fall of communism in 1989, sugar production from 1996 should fully cover Slovakia's 1997 domestic consumption, estimated at around 190,000 to 205,000 tonnes.
"This will allow us to export the surplus production, something between 20,000 to 25,000 tonnes," Palacka said.
The 1996 sugar beet crop totalled 1.78 million tonnes from a sown area of 42,100 hectares. The average yield per hectare was 40.7 tonnes. The sugar content per beet was 15.5 percent, Palacka said.
He declined to disclose forecasts for this year's sugar production, but said that the sown area should rise by 20 percent to around 50,100 hectares.
